Implementation inference from [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163): for every valid next-item target, extract its preceding ≤10 raw items, left-pad to length 10, and run the same causal dilated residual network; score only the final position. Enumerate all targets, microbatch these windows, and retain one shared model. Cropping hidden states from a full-sequence pass is insufficient: they may already encode older items. Independent windows enforce the bound regardless of receptive field. Use identical padding, masking and positional conventions during prediction. Translation equivalence requires no absolute-position dependence and matching boundaries; biases/normalization can make padded hidden states nonzero. Equivalence to ordinary sequence encoding holds only where its entire effective receptive field and boundary behavior match the window.

For N valid targets per original optimizer batch, zero gradients once, then backpropagate each microbatch’s summed target losses divided by N. This gives the position-mean gradient of the complete window batch, up to floating-point differences; dividing microbatch means equally fails for uneven sizes. Keep weights fixed throughout accumulation; clip and step once afterward. With AMP, keep the scaler constant and unscale only after accumulation. [PyTorch guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/amp_examples.html). Tokenwise LayerNorm preserves sample independence; batch-dependent normalization does not. Dropout generally changes realized gradients across batching arrangements; matching random masks is necessary for numerical equivalence. Independent masks preserve the expected additive objective, while changing cross-target gradient correlations versus shared sequence activations.

Derived convolution cost, with D layers, width H and kernel K: ordinary B×L training costs O(BLDKH²); independent windows cost O(N·10·DKH²), approximately tenfold when N≈BL. Microbatching reduces activation memory to O(m·10·DH), without removing repeated computation; output scoring remains once per target. Lazy window gathering avoids materializing all windows. Kernel-launch overhead and lost activation reuse can further increase runtime.
